featured_reviews.name: Siddhesh Kotian
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Third Wave Café in Vile Parle just yesterday, and while there were a few highlights, the overall experience left room for improvement.

Parking:
One of the first challenges we faced was parking. There’s no dedicated parking for the café, and you’re left to hunt for a spot nearby. With MTP odd-even parking rules in place, it gets even trickier. Be cautious — incorrect parking here can lead to hefty fines from the Maharashtra Traffic Police.

Ambience & Crowd:
When we entered, the café wasn’t too crowded — just a couple of tables were occupied. So, we expected a smooth and quick service experience.

Service:
Unfortunately, the service was disappointing. Despite the café being nearly empty, we had to wait 20–25 minutes for our order. The staff seemed distracted and unresponsive — even when we tried to call them over, it felt like they were in their own world. This slow and inattentive service really took away from the overall experience, especially since we were quite hungry.

Food:
On the brighter side, the food was excellent. We ordered the Chicken Tikka Roll and Paneer Tikka Roll — both were served in good quantity and tasted delicious. The flavors were spot on, and the food was definitely the highlight of our visit.

Final Thoughts:
If you’re visiting for the food, you won’t be disappointed — it’s tasty and filling. But be prepared for slow service and no parking options. Hopefully, the management takes steps to improve the service quality, because the food truly deserves better support.

featured_reviews.review_text:
AB Cafe, Vile Parle is a small neighborhood café that delivers a basic coffee experience but falls short in a few areas.

Food:
Tried their hot chocolate, which was decent but nothing special. Also ordered the Irish cappuccino and Irish cold coffee, but found them to be average and lacking the richness or punch you'd expect from Irish variants. Overall, the drinks were okay but not something I’d go back specifically for.

Service:
The café is typically run by a single person managing orders, billing, and coffee preparation. This setup often leads to slow service if there are more than a couple of customers. While the person is courteous, it feels understaffed for smooth operations.

Ambiance:
The place is compact and gets cramped easily, even during non-peak hours. A nice gesture is the availability of board games like chess, but sadly, they are poorly maintained — the chess board had food stains and looked unclean. While the idea is good, poor upkeep makes it less enjoyable.

Overall:
A basic neighborhood coffee spot — works if you need a quick caffeine fix in Vile Parle, but neither the coffee nor the ambiance is something that stands out. The place has potential if they improve the service speed, space management, and maintain small touches like better board games.

featured_reviews.name: Anirban S (an1rb6n)
featured_reviews.review_text:
This is a hard place to review. I was constantly torned between small misses here and there, and then they had something to offer to compensate. Overall, in the price point, it was a brilliant place to have breakfast. Since we only had breakfast buffet, my review is restricted to it.
Food options are plenty. There is a lot of variety available. In fact you can specifically request certain tweaks in them too. But the options at times are just weird in terms of placement. For example artisalan breads did not have the toaster near it. Near the toaster (and I found only 1 toaster) there was no bread. Once toasted the only spreads available is butter and jam. But they have waffle station which has all the spreads available. This is the operational planning lapse. But at the same time, they were kind enough to serve the bread on the table when requested. And they cooked up and awesome egg benedict. Since I don't care about dosa, idly, vada etc. - the cold cuts, ham, chorizo, chicken were good. The mixed miso soup with prawns were amazing. But the only variety of chicken as dish was the indianized chinese version of it. It's not inherently bad, but suprising to me a bit. Marriott after all 😅.
But I understand they are focused on the needs of the people, who would want these generalized dishes. I didn't find almost anyone else even near the hummas, or the pork sausages. Safe to say the target customers and my appetite (since I'm from Kolkata) were heaven and hell apart. But the spread was well balanced. They had a really good pineapple juice. But they didn't have the grape juice or it was like it'll take some time. But the pastries were really tasty. But for yogart they only had epigamia which was odd.
Small gaps here and there, but at the price point on a Sunday morning it was a superb brunch. Food were tasty, plenty, warm and overall good. Not extraordinary, but good.
Note, they close the breakfast by 11AM mostly, so reach early if you plan to taste a lot of items. But definitely worth a revisit.

Horrible menu planning. Being ex hospitality professionals we took a stroll and took a look of /at the buffet spread.
Everything seemed just ok !!!

But when every dish was tried and tasted  , nothing hit right to the palate.

I mean if one is spending around 6k plus for 2 people for a dinner buffet, the least you could do is keep varieties , offer mutton on the main course but no...no varieties , infact itseems the headchef who planned this menu wasn't interested in tasting the laid out food...and just for the sake of it and cost consciously kept less options thereby making the guest unsatisfied for his/her desire to try out varieties .

Being a weekend ( Saturday) and such pathetic buffet option is laid out then might as well shut down your buffet. ...better options are available with standalone restaurants in and around the vicinity.
Had come here to celebrate a birthday and was just left disappointed. Never coming back again for sure...

With regards to service , I must say the SERVICE  PERSONNELS were attentive to clearing the tables and refilling our water glasses. So kudos to the service team, but the kitchen team and its head needs to evaluate their menu and revamp the buffet menu.

Last but not the least...when it comes to food, if a guest is disappointed, the guest will definitely not come back again. so I guess you guys lost a customer .
Pathetic experience!!!!
Not recommended!!!

featured_reviews.name: Siddhesh Kotian
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Garde Manger Café in Vile Parle East, and while the food was enjoyable, the overall experience was far from satisfying.

Parking:
As with many cafés in this area, there is no dedicated parking available. Visitors traveling by car or bike should be prepared to look around for legal street parking — not very convenient.

Seating & Ambience:
The café offers both indoor and outdoor seating, but the space feels very tight and congested. The tables are extremely small — if you’re planning to order multiple dishes, you’ll struggle to fit everything on the table at once. It gets uncomfortable quickly.

Also, the tables are placed too close to each other, and when the café is full, the noise levels can be overwhelming. During our visit, there was a loud group nearby, and due to the cramped layout, it was hard to have a peaceful conversation or enjoy our food.

Service:
The service was slow and poorly coordinated. We ordered hummus with pita bread, and although we had already finished most of our meal, the pita bread hadn’t arrived. When we followed up, it was clear from the staff’s expressions that they had forgotten to place the order. It eventually arrived after a wait of 30+ minutes, which really disrupted the flow of our meal.

Food:
On the positive side, the food was genuinely good — tasty and fresh. The flavors were spot on, and if I had to rate just the food, I’d give it a thumbs-up.

⸻

Final Thoughts:
While the food is worth trying, the lack of space, poor service, and noisy environment took away from what could have been a nice café experience. I hope the management considers expanding the space and training the staff better to handle orders and communication.

Boulevard is one of the famous restaurant since ages. Orchid can be easily said to be one of the best ecotel hotel since years. Buffet of them had really lot of options. View from the restaurant is excellent too. Certainly a must visit restaurant if you want to enjoy the lavish spread. Strongly recommend, go for it.

Location- This restaurant is on the first floor of very famous ecotel hotel Orchid. Orchid is just adjacent to the domestic airport.(5/5)

Theme- Being the main restaurant of the hotel it's 24*7, it serves mix cuisine with a la carte and buffet both.(5/5)

Ambience- one side of first floor is occupied by this restaurant so yes it's really big. Divided into small sections. You can get a lobby view from any table.  One side of restaurant they got lovely spreaded buffet . Lighting is bright n fresh. Got mix tables or 2,4,8 covers. Soft music at background was nice.(5/5)

Food- This being a main restaurant of the hotel, it is open 24*7. You either can go for a la carte menu or decide to go with the lavish buffet spread. We decided to hog on buffet which looked really impressive.  Buffet consist of soup, salads, farsaan,starters, Chaat counter, main courses, desserts.(5/5)

Soup was the first dish I tastes and was highly impressive with the taste of it. It was seafood clear soup which was made with fish stock, fish chunks, thick sliced celery. Great way to start.
Chaat counter had various options like seven Puri, dahi Puri, dahi wada, bhel. You have to order your dish to the chef who was standing on the counter and he will send it to your table.
I had a go at dahi Puri which was delicious.

Starters they had paneer Tikka, corn bruschetta, fish fingers, chicken in Asian style. Fish finger was the dish I kept eating for long, fresh fish and crispy enough.

Salad counter had mix of veg and nonveg salads, loved the smoked salmon salad and tuna potato salad.
Very rare that I saw a farsaan options in multicuisine restaurant of 5*. They were serving bakerwadi and khokla, I didn't try it though was looking tempting.
Same section had options of nachos with in-house cheese sauce.

Main course really had many options. Pasta  live counter seemed very busy. I opted for more Indian food as awadhi gosht korma caught my attention. Excellent colour with medium thickness gravy and well cooked lamb in it was heaven with the butter naan (any bread options you like) which they serve on table.
Dishes like Pan seared fish with garlic cilantro butter sauce, chicken in black bean sauce were a must try.
Coming to rice , I saw Chicken biryani  first time itself when was checking the buffet. So took biryani with some for a gravy. Biryani was well made with long grain rice, garnished well with fried onions and had extraordinary aroma of it's own, Enjoyed it.

Dessert section is always said to be the best part of any buffet, it's true. Here they had mix if Indian and continental desserts. Had dark chocolate mousse, kiwi mousse, peach apricot jelly, Chocolate mud cake , strawberry salsa with caramel mousse etc. Had ice cream options along with black current Halwa and kesari kheer.

Ambiance:

Service:

Food and Coffee:

Service Incident:
Regrettably, my experience was marred by an incident that occurred during my visit. Despite specifically ordering a combo, I did not receive the combo. To add to the disappointment, I was later asked to pay extra for the item. This lack of attention to detail and the subsequent inconvenience significantly impacted my overall perception of the cafe.

In conclusion, Blue Tokai has the potential to become a great cafe, but there are several areas that need improvement. While the coffee and food were commendable, the lackluster ambiance, poorly trained staff, and the service mishap prevented me from giving it a higher rating.
